A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LayeredDepth research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including the additional supplementary material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-layer baseline experiments, single-layer benchmarking and fine-tuning results in Tables 1–3, plus an annotation-validation experiment in Section 9.1.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds comparisons with transparency-specific methods and Depth Anything V2 multi-layer fine-tuning results, including Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: Section 9.2.1 adds a Depth Anything V2 multi-layer adaptation that replicates its depth head four times and fine-tunes it. This extends the existing multi-head approach; the three NeWCRFs designs, synthetic generator, and stated loss remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Section 4.2 adds nonexistent-layer test cases, such as a second layer in an opaque region, extending evaluation to rejecting invalid depth predictions. The underlying coverage remains the same 1,500 real images and 15,300 synthetic images; the additional model experiments introduce no new dataset or domain.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add the transparency-specific Depth4ToM and Tosi et al. methods alongside the retained general-depth comparators. The appendix also adds a fine-tuned Depth Anything V2 multi-head comparator to the NeWCRFs multi-layer comparisons, substantially broadening the comparative evidence.

E3.justification: v2 introduces 10% manually labeled fake tuples, scored incorrect when a model predicts depth at nonexistent layers. Reported annotation counts change from 1.7M/4.2M/4.2M pairs/triplets/quadruplets to 2.5M/5.9M/5.8M. It also adds Depth Anything V2 fine-tuning and per-layer synthetic evaluation. The real and synthetic image splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 9–13 extend qualitative case comparisons across real and synthetic scenes, including side-by-side multi-layer predictions and synthetic ground truth. These provide additional evidence about layer separation and boundary/deeper-layer artifacts. No controlled ablation, sensitivity study, or dedicated robustness test is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The annotation check using 30 synthetic images and reporting 98% agreement is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes extensively: Index Concat's Layer 7 quadruplet accuracy changes from 77.64% to 45.08% alongside the revised evaluation, so this is not a same-setting performance decline. Tables 2–3 add comparator results, and Tables 4–5 add multi-layer results, including Depth Anything V2's 61.68% overall quadruplet accuracy. Existing single-layer comparator scores are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same definitions of layers as medium transitions and depth as an ordered sequence of camera-axis distances. No new theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption appears; the fake-tuple addition is an empirical scoring rule.

C1.justification: The introduction and contribution list expand the stated benchmark size from 10.2M to 14.2M relative-depth tuples. The central task and dataset novelty claims, synthetic-to-real generalization claim, and headline Metric3D V2 improvement from 55.14% to 75.20% remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 removes Section 7.1's speculation that index prompting explains especially strong Layer 7 performance. Section 9.2.1 adds interpretation of the Depth Anything V2 results as evidence of synthetic-to-real generalization, while acknowledging remaining boundary and deeper-layer artifacts.

D1.justification: The appendix adds explicit input/output channel specifications, Depth Anything V2 head replication, and fake-annotation counts. It omits v1's explicit distinction between ground-truth recurrent inputs during training and predicted inputs during inference; this omission does not establish a procedural change. Appendix release wording also becomes less definite, despite retained availability claims in the abstract.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Costanzino et al.'s Depth4ToM and Tosi et al.'s diffusion-based depth method, positioning them as transparency-specific comparators in Section 7.2. The related-work discussion and broader dataset novelty positioning otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose is retained. The appendix is reorganized into Additional Details and Additional Results, training explanations are expanded, the conclusion is shortened, and author emails are added. These are localized edits rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with five comparative galleries in Figures 9–13 and two appendix tables. Table 4 redisplays Table 1's revised rows alongside Depth Anything V2, while Table 5 presents new synthetic multi-layer results. Tables 2–3 gain comparator columns/rows; the original figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The nonexistent-layer check improves evaluation relevance, while transparency-specific comparators and additional real/synthetic multi-layer evidence strengthen the assessment of dataset utility. These are useful gains over v1, but documentation remains incomplete: the new Depth Anything V2 fine-tuning settings are sparse, the recurrent training/inference clarification is lost, and the discussion does not address Depth4ToM's higher quadruplet score than Depth Anything V2 in the expanded Table 2.
